note: (Kakajirna, Thuillier) Inst. Nat. d'Hyg.. Un. de Rech, de Neuro-Psycho-Fharm, Parie
title: Eeg effects of psychoanaleptics and biogenic amine precursors in reserpinized rabbits
abstract: Different antidepressant substances do not all have the same effect on rabbit EEG. While imipramine and serotonin produce analogous and psilocybin similar changes in the EEG1 mefexamide and TOPA do not cause any anomalies at all. The possible relationship of these anomalies to tryptaminergic effects, which are found in certain antidepressants and not in others, is discussed. (IIC, 8a).

tertiary_title: De LSD-controverse
author_address: R.F.J. Brocker, Crayenesterlaan 126, Haarlem, Netherlands
note: (Brocker) Crayenesterlaan 126, Haarlem, Netherlands
title: The LSD-controversy
abstract: As a result of press and television publicity, psycholytics have been increasingly brought to the attention of the general public both at home and abroad. In a letter to the Editor of this journal, Sandoz have announced that they only supply LSD and psilocybin to psychiatrists in exceptional cases. After a brief survey of scientific research in this field, the therapeutic and religious speculations which have given rise to a serious controversy among psychiatrists on the advantages and disadvantages of psycholytic therapy are discussed. Two cases treated with LSD are reported. A hypothesis on the psychologic effect of these drugs is framed, which may also serve to elucidate the possible backgrounds of this dispute.

author_address: G.M. Maxwell, Dept. of Child Hlth, Univ. of Adelaide
note: (Maxwell) Dept. of Child Hlth, Univ. of Adelaide
journal_name: Archives internationales de pharmacodynamie et de therapie
title: The effects of tryptamine and alpha-methyl-tryptamine on the general and coronary haemodynamics and metabolism of the dog
abstract: Cardiac output (Fick), and coronary flow (N2O Fick) were measured before and after infusion of tryptamine or a- methyltryptamine. Both drugs were found to increase cardiac output, and systemic and pulmonary arterial mean blood pressures. Coronary flow also increased, and, with tryptamine, an increase in coronary sinus oxygen content was recorded. Some of the properties of serotonin, or-methyltryptamine, and psilocybin are also present in the simpler compound tryptamine. (IIC, 18).

tertiary_title: Modification de seuil convulsivant du bemegride par les drogues psychotropes
author_address: H. Nakajima, Unite de Neuro-Psychopharm. INSERM, Hop. Sainte Anne, Paris
note: (Nakajima, Granjean, Thuillier) Unite de Neuro-Psychopharm. INSERM, Hop. Sainte Anne, Paris
title: Modification of the convulsion-threshold of bemegride by psychotropic drugs
abstract: The convulsion-threshold of bemegride in the rabbit ranges from. 13 to 15 mg./kg. If the animals is given resrpine, conveisions will appear with doses as low 0-7 mg./kg. Methamphetamine, 5-hydroxytryptophan, psilocybin and imipramine protect the reserpinized animal against bexnegriae-induced convulsions.

tertiary_title: Evolution de nos connaissances sur les principes toxiques des champignons superieurs
author_address: Fac. de Pharm., Paris
note: (Deysson) Fac. de Pharm., Paris
title: Advancement of knowledge of toxic components of higher fungi
abstract: A review covering Amanita phalloides cyclopeptides, fungi causing a paraphalloidal syndrome, toxic components of Amanita muscaria and Amanita pantherina and the psychotomimetic indole derivatives psilocin and psilocybine.

author_address: Exp. Pharmacol. Div., Inst. of Physiol., Univ. of Glasgow
note: (Lewis, Ritchie, Van Petten) Exp. Pharmacol. Div., Inst. of Physiol., Univ. of Glasgow
title: The influence of hallucinogenic drugs upon in vivo brain levels of adenine nucleotides, phosphocreatine and inorganic phosphate in the rat
abstract: The effects upon rat brain levels of adenine nucleotides, phosphocreatine and inorganic phosphate of injecting lysergide, psilocybin, mescaline, bufotenine, JB 329, hyoscine, atropine, cocaine, dopa and 5-hydroxytryptophan have been studied. With the exceptions of dopa and 5-hydroxytryptophan, all drugs raised ATP levels and the ATP/ADP ratio, and, except for 5-hydroxytryptophan, atropine and cocaine, the phosphocreatine levels. Only hyoscine caused a significant rise in the inorganic phosphate concentrations. The other drugs did not change the phosphate content. There appears to be some relationship between the ability to cause behavioral stimulation in the rat and to produce increased levels of labile energy-yielding phosphates in brain tissue.

tertiary_title: Effets de certains hallucinogenes sur l'electroencephalogramme et le comportement conditionne du lapin
author_address: Ist. Sup. di Sanita, Roma
note: (Baran, Longo) Ist. Sup. di Sanita, Roma
title: Effects of psychomimetic drugs on EEG and conditioned behavior in rabbit
abstract: Behavioral and EEG effects of various psychomimetic drugs were studied in rabbit. Action on electrical activity and cardiovascular system was studied on acute preparations. On chronical preparations EEG effects were studied and compared with spontaneous behavior variations. On specially trained animals the influence of the drugs on a discrimination conditioned exercise was compared with EEG effects. The drugs studied were tryptamine, dimethyltryptamine, diethyltryptamine, bufotenine, psilocybine and mescaline. On the EEG all the drugs induced a disappearance of hippocampal (theta) rhythm. The most active drug was psilocybine, and the least one is mescaline, which induced modifications of the EEG only at doses of 75 mg./ kg. Generally, these drugs influence discrimination conditioned exercise with doses lower than those having an effect on the EEG. Analysis of effects on EEG and behavior confirmed that these drugs have their own characteristics, which distinguish them from other drugs (sympathomimetic amines, analeptics, convulsants) and which allow them to be classified in the same class as lysergide (LSD).

author_address: M.H. Keeler, Dept. of Psychiat., Univ. of North Carolina, Sch. of Med., Chapel Hill, NC, United States
note: (Keeler) Dept. of Psychiat., Univ. of North Carolina, Sch. of Med., Chapel Hill, NC, United States
title: The effects of psilocybin on a test of after-image perception
abstract: After-image perception is measured by competition of a colored light with white light of different intensity. A list of spontaneous visual responses is answered by the participants in the trial. In double blind experiments either 2 mg. per kg. of psilocybin or a placebo was given orally. Correlation between results after psilocybin of the 2 series is 0.88 (p<0.001). A tentative hypothesis is offered that a relative decrease in inhibitory as compared to excitatory reactivity in cone-based processes might favor the imagery of visions.

author_address: A.M. Ludwig, Mendota State Hosp., Madison, WI, United States
note: (Ludwig, Levine) Mendota State Hosp., Madison, WI, United States
title: Patterns of hallucinogenic drug abuse
abstract: This report of hallucinogenic drug abuse is based on extensive interviews with 26 patients who have used these drugs and one patient who had intimate knowledge of their illicit use. The most frequently abused substance was found to be peyote, folowed closely by mescaline, with LSD and psilocybin far less frequently used. Availability of these agents was sporadic and, in general, limited to large cities. Their distribution, economics, and pattern of use were different than those of the opiate drugs, and the greatest number of people who abused them also used marijuana, amphetamines, and barbiturates. The hallucinogenic drugs' addiction potential, dangers, and influence on sexual function are also reported.

author_address: L.E. Hollister, Dept. of Med., Stanford Univ. Sch. of Med., Palo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hollister, Sjoberg) Dept. of Med., Stanford Univ. Sch. of Med., Palo Alto, CA, United States
title: Clinical syndromes and biochemical alterations following mescaline. Lysergic acid diethylamide, psilocybin and a combination of the three psychotomimetic drugs
abstract: Twenty-four volunteer subjects were treated with mescaline (5 mg./K), LSD -25 (1.5 meg./K), psilocybin (225 meg./K) or a combination of all 3 drugs using one-third doses of each. The 1 treatments were given orally in a latin-square order. Clinical effects as assessed by a 75-item questionnaire, the Clyde Mood Scale and the Hof fer-Osmund Diagnostic (HOD) test were remarkably alike for all 4 treatments. Somatic effects or varying degrees of intellectual impairment were most apparent on the questionnaire: many perceptual and psychic symptoms were denied. Of the 6 factors on the Clyde Mood Scale, 3 (friendly, energetic and clearthinking) were uniformly decreased by the drugs in the first 2 to 4 hours; 3 other factors (aggressive, jittery and depressed) tended to be increased by the drugs, both early and late. Questions most often answered positively on the HOD test were concerned with somatic effects or perceptual alterations (fluctuating time sense, increased auditory and tactile acuity, and visual effects); once again, frankly psychotic symptoms were seldom reported. All treatments increased plasma free fatty acids, but the degree of mobilization of FFA was not related to the severity of the clinical reaction. All treatments decreased urinary creatinine clearance slightly; clearance of inorganic phosphorus was more substantially reduced, along with increased serum phosphorus. Little effect was noted on urinary calcium excretion, serum calcium, plasma glucose, or serum triglycerides. Levels of circulating eosinophils declined, but not to a significant degree. The biochemical alterations probably represent nonspecific reactions to stress.

tertiary_title: O Janetove psychastenii
author_address: Th. Dosuzkov, Logoped.Odd. DFN, Praha
note: (Dosuzkov) Logoped.Odd. DFN, Praha
title: On janet's psychasthenia
abstract: Janet's description of psychasthenia lacks a basic syndrome, a clinical course of the disorder and its pathogenetic mechanisms. It is no more than a group of symptoms which Janet did not consider hysterical and may also be present in other neuroses and psychoses (except paranoia). The notion of psychasthenia as a clinical, and even more so as a nosological entity is rejected. It is assumed to be a variety of psychopathy and schizophrenia.

author_address: E.J. Tolan, Columbus State Hosp., Columbus, OH, United States
note: (Tolan, Lingl) Columbus State Hosp., Columbus, OH, United States
title: 'Model psychosis' produced by inhalation of gasoline fumes
abstract: Two teen-age cases of toxic psychosis associated with gasoline inhalation are described and compared with the so-called 'model psychoses' evoked by mescaline. LSD -25 and psilocybin. The symptoms were predominantly autonomic, perceptual and affective. The perceptual experiences included mucn personally significant symbolic content. The inhaling of gasoline quickly became a tempting recurrent activity in the case of these two boys with maladjusted and impulsive personalities.

tertiary_title: K problematice optickych poruch v autoexperimentech s halucinogeny
author_address: S. Grof, Vyz. Ust. Psychiat., Praha, Czech Republic
note: (Grof) Vyz. Ust. Psychiat., Praha, Czech Republic
title: The problem of optic disturbances in auto-experiments with hallucinogens
abstract: This paper summarizes personal introspective observations of disturbed optic perception in auto-experiments with 3 hallucinogens (LSD-25, mescaline, psilocybine). The dynamics and development of these disorders are described and attention is drawn to the difference between phenomena observed with the eyes closed and with the eyes open. Experiments with small doses of the preparation and the period of onset and recession of psychotic changes are particularly suited for these observations as under these conditions the illusions and pseudohallucinations do not arise spontaneously but only when the eyes are fixed and when the subject collaborates actively. Attention is drawn to the analogy between the mechanism of the genesis of optic disturbances in model psychoses and the search for different interpretations in Rorschach's tables. This analogy is demonstrated by a comparison of the graphic records of successive illusory transformations of a single object during LSD psychosis and some specimens of a drawn Rorschach protocol. In conclusion the importance of the mechanism described is discussed for the understanding of the pathoplastic aspect of model psychoses and the relationship of some observed phenomena to the problem of naturally occurring mental disorders.

author_address: D. Ub Ans K B, Med. Fak., Palack Univ., Olomouc, Tschechoslowakei
note: (Ub Ans K B, Kilaffk, VyhnankovaM, Sevctk) Med. Fak., Palack Univ., Olomouc, Tschechoslowakei
title: Trials with psilocybin administration in organic cerebra amage. v. significance and value of psilocybin in clinical neur ology (german)
abstract: Besides in experimental neurology, this drug, in small doses, may be of therapeutic value in cases of anxiety and depression accompanying organic brain lesions, and in speech rehabilitation of some forms of T)hsia.

tertiary_title: Versuchsapplikation von psilocybin bei organischen hirnschadigungen. iii. ergebnisse experimenteller untersuchungsmethoden assoziationsexperiment, methode kunstlicher wortverbindungen
author_address: M. Vyhnankovi, Med.-Fak, Pa Lac k Univ., Olomouc, Tscheche Slowakei
note: (Vyhnankovi, Rfigigkova, Dubansk, Kolaffk, Sevifk) Med.-Fak, Pa Lac k Univ., Olomouc, Tscheche Slowakei
title: Trials with psilocybin administration in organic cerebral damage. iii. results of tests (association test; artificial word-combination method)
abstract: Clinical results were rather inconsistent, but a certain stimulatory and normalizing effect on persistent pathologic inhibitions of speech appeared to be demonstrated.

tertiary_title: Versuchsapplikation von psilocybin bei organischen hirnschadigungen. ii. somatische und psychische wirkungen in unserem krankengut und bei gesunden versuchspersonen
author_address: B. Dubansk, Med. Fak., Palack Univ., Olomouc, Tschechoslowakei
note: (Dubansk, Vyh Nenkova, Kolaffk, Sevoik, Rftziakova) Med. Fak., Palack Univ., Olomouc, Tschechoslowakei
title: Trials with psilocybin administration in organic cerebral damage. u. somatic and mental effects in patients and normal subjects
abstract: Psilocybin was given in doses of ca 0.15 mg./kg. orally or B.C. to neurologic patients and normal persons. Severe occipital lesions and increased intracranial pressure inhibit the visual effects of the drug. In normal persons a disordered body image and signs of depersonalization were noted.

tertiary_title: Versuchsapplikation von psilocybin bei organischen hirnschadigungen. i. psychotomimetische wirkungen von psilocybin und von den ubrigen phantastika
author_address: B. Dubansk, Med. Pak, Palack Univ., Olomouc, Tschechoslowakei
note: (Dubansk, Vyhnankova, Kolarfk, Sevfk) Med. Pak, Palack Univ., Olomouc, Tschechoslowakei
title: Trials with psilocybin administration in organic cerebra amage. i. psychotomimetic actions of psilocybin and other hallucinogens
abstract: Review of chemical, pharmacological and psychotoraimetic proportion of psilocybin, mescaline, lysergide and related substances, and a number of drugs of natural an ynthetic origin, with delirogenie activity.

tertiary_title: Caracterisation et detection pharraacologiques des substances hallucinogenes. ii. antagonismes vis-a-vis de la morphine chez la souris
author_address: J. Jacob, Lab. de Pharmacol., Serv. de Chim. Ther., Inst. Pasteur, Paris
note: (Jacob, Loiseau, Echinard- Garin, Barthelemy, Lafille) Lab. de Pharmacol., Serv. de Chim. Ther., Inst. Pasteur, Paris
journal_name: Archives internationales de pharmacodynamie et de therapie
title: Pharmacological characterization and detection of psy-chotomimetic agents. ii. morphine antagonism in mice
abstract: Effects of psychotomimetic drugs on morphinized mice were examined by the hotplate method. The drugs were administered s. c. 30 min. before morphine and 1 hr. before the first exposure. Two reactions were studied, (a) A simple one: licking at the first exposure (dose of morphine 10 mg. /kg., s. c. ) and (b) a more elaborate one: jumping at the 3rd exposure (dose of morphine 1 mg. /kg. s.c. ). Effects varied with the drug, dosage and reaction. For lysergide, bromolysergide, psilocybine, dimethyl- and diethyltryptamines, nalorphine, and mescaline, the main effect was shortening of the licking times and often, for similar or higher doses, of the jumping times. The potencies in reducing the effect of morphine on licking correlated cept for nalorphine which induces hypothermia, with their hyperthermic activities in the rabbit, as determined previously (Jacob and Lafille). 'JB 318' and 'JB 336', two piperidyl diphenylglycolates, also reduced reaction times of morphinized mice but they differed from the aforementioned compounds in being more potent on the 'jumping' than on the 'licking' reaction, a property shared also by scopolamine. Dinitrophenol and pentetrazole were almost ineffective whereas DL-amphetamine and phencyclidine further increased the reaction times. Mechanisms of action and value of these 2 tests for screening and characterization of psychotomimetic agents are discussed.

tertiary_title: Studio clinico e psicopatologico della psilocibina
author_address: G.C. Reda, Clin. delle Mal. Nerv. e Ment., Univ. di Roma
note: (Reda, Vella, Cancrini, D'Agostino) Clin. delle Mal. Nerv. e Ment., Univ. di Roma
title: A clinical and psychopathological study of psilocybin
abstract: The results of previous researches on the somatic, psychological and psychopatho-logical effects of psilocybin on animals and humans are summarized. The EEG changes are examined in particular; the effects of psilocybin are compared with those of LSD 25 and mescalin; the simple and crossed 'tolerance' of these drugs are also studied. The vegetative, psychological and psychopathological effects are also discussed based on the intramuscular administration of psilocybin (3-12 mz in repeated doses) to 21 psychiatric (psychotic and neurotic) women patients. The first trials to assess therapeutic ally the 'cathartic' action of psilocybin on some psychoneurotic women are described. The personal reports of 2 healthy volunteers are also included.

tertiary_title: Nasa klinicka iskustva sa novim psihofarmakom psilocybin-om
author_address: D. Dordevic, Clin. for Neurol. and Psychiat. Dis., VMA, Belgrade
note: (Dordevic) Clin. for Neurol. and Psychiat. Dis., VMA, Belgrade
title: Clinical experiences with the new psychodrug psilocybin
abstract: The drug was administered subcutaneously to a group of 30 hospitalized neurotics, in doses of 3-6 mg., 2 to 4 times a day. Considerable clinical improvement was seen in 53% of all patients treated, especially in acute depressive neurotic reactions. Owing to its ability to recall to consciousness forgotten and unpleasant experiences and conflicts, and to its euphoric effect, psilocybin is an excellent adjuvant in psychotherapeutic procedures. The individual reaction to psilocybin varies. It depends on the intellect of the patient and on his readiness to elaborate on the material that he has re-experienced. The patient does not develop tolerance to the drug, nor have addiction or complications been encountered.

author_address: L.E. Hollister, Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hollister) Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
journal_name: Archives internationales de pharmacodynamie et de therapie
title: Effect of centrally-acting drugs on mobilization of free fatty acids
abstract: Changes in plasma FFA levels following acute doses of a series of central nervous system drugs were used to group these agents. Each drug class used, antidepressants, antipsychotics and psychotomimetics, increased FFA levels to some degree. Elevations was least with drugs having sedative effects, which included both the phenothiazine tranquilizers, chlorpromazine and thioridazine, as well as the dibenzazepine antidepressants, imipramine and desmethylimipramine. Increases were greater with excitant drugs, such as the antipsychotics, reserpine and benzquinamide, or the psychotomimetics, lysergide, mescaline and psilocybin. Effects of centrally-acting drugs on plasma FFA levels do not provide clues to their clinical therapeutic effects, though the degree of elevation of FFA levels seems related to stimulant as opposed to sedative properties.

tertiary_title: Caracterisation et detection pharmacologiques des substances hallucinogenes. I. Activites hyperthermisantes chez le lapin
author_address: J. Jacob, Lab. de Pharmacol., Serv. de Chim, TherapeuU Inst. Pasteur, Paris
note: (Jacob, Lafille) Lab. de Pharmacol., Serv. de Chim, TherapeuU Inst. Pasteur, Paris
journal_name: Archives internationales de pharmacodynamie et de therapie
title: PHARMACOLOGICAL DETECTION and CHARACTERIZATION of HALLUCINOGENS. I. HYPERTHERMIZING ACTIVITIES in THE RABBIT
abstract: Hyperthermic actions together with their time and dose effect relationships have been determined in rabbits for different hallucinogenic agents, either of the essential type (lysergide, psilocybine, mescaline, dimethyl- and diethyltryptamines, N-ethyl-3-piperidyl benzilate ('JB 318') and an analogue ('JB 336'), nalorphine and phencyclidine) or of the contingent type (bromolysergide, alpha-ethyltryptamine, amphetamine). Pentetrazole and dinitrophenol have also been studied. All the hallucinogenic s studied raised the temperature, the only exception being nalorphine. Effects increased regularly with dosages except for bromolysergide whose action, on the contrary, subsided, and for phencyclidine. No characteristic permits, without further study, to distinguish between the action of hallucinogenic and that of dinitrophenol. Hyperthermic activity does thus not appear to be a necessary or sufficient characteristic of all hallucinogenic agents. Nevertheless, a fair quantitative correlation has been found between both activities, for compounds with actual or potential indole structure: lysergide, bromolysergide, psilocybine, dimethyl- and diethyltryptamines and mescaline. The 2 piperidyl benzilates ('JB 318' and 'JB 336') behave, in both activities, as intermediates between the tryptamines and mescaline. However, their position on the correlation diaphragm discloses a relatively too low hyperthermic activity; this suggests a possible different modality of hallucinogenic action. Mydriatic activity did not correlate with the other 2, as mescaline was, on the contrary, found to be miotic. With due allowance for aberrant actions (negative with nalorphine, positive with dinitrophenol) the test of hyperthermia appears thus as one of a battery for preclinical detection and even, in some chemical series, quantitative evaluation of hallucinogenic properties. Its advantages are: its ability to give information for both predominant action and side effect and its experimental simplicity, this latter being illustrated by a screening schedule already applied to series of synthetics. Other tests will be described in a following publication. (II, 8).

author_address: A.M. Hartman, Vet. Adm. Hosp., PaIo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hartman, Hollister) Vet. Adm. Hosp., PaIo Alto, CA, United States
title: Effect of mescaline, lysergic acid diethylamide and psilocybin on color perception
abstract: Twenty subjects were given 3 psychotomimetic drugs (mescaline, LSD-25 and psilocybin) in fixed doses, 18 receiving all 3. Colour experience was tested by applying stimuli involving colour perception, stimuli eliciting subjective colours, and stimuli usually devoid of visual experience. Almost all measures of colour perception were affected. Hue discrimination was decreased significantly by psilocybin, to a slightly lesser extent by the other two drugs. Colour reports in afterimages were significantly increased by all 3 drugs, but duration of after-image was increased significantly only by psilocybin. Elicitation of subjective colours from flicker was increased by all 3 drugs, significantly more by mescaline and LSD-25 than by psilocybin. The combination of flicker and pure tones evoked more colour reports than flicker alone. The increase was significant only after LSD-25, no significant differences being demonstrated between the effects of the 3 drugs. Visual effects, both colours and patterns, elicited by pure tones were signiiicantly increased by LSD and mescaline, though these effects were not great at cne doses used in this study. Spectral patterns of evoked colours varied slightly between the 3 drugs. These results are interpreted as indicating that stimuli which evoke subjective colour phenomena, or even those not usually associated with visual phenomena, are enhanced by psychotomimetics. On the other hand, the usual perception of colour, as judged by hue discrimination, may actually be slightly decreased.

author_address: M. Knoll, Inst. fur Techn. Elekt., Techn. Hochsch., Munchen, Germany
note: (Knoll, Kugler, Hofer, Lawder) Inst. fur Techn. Elekt., Techn. Hochsch., Munchen, Germany
title: Effects of chemical stimulation of electrically-induced phosphenes on their bandwidth, shape, number and intensity
abstract: It has been shown in earlier work that 'phosphenes' (luminescent endogenous patterns experienced with closed eyes) may occur not only during drowsiness, shock, fasting, meditation, deprivation of sensory signals or chemical intoxication but also during and after stimulation of the brain from cranial electrodes by rectangular electric pulses mainly within the EEG frequency range (1 to 30 c./sec.). Because of their relatively narrow bandwidth, it was possible to distinguish up to 12 different electrically-induced patterns per individual. Furthermore, it has been found that the same individual may experience the same phosphene pattern at different stimulation frequencies. Particular patterns may remain stable for at least 6 months. For checking the effect of additional chemical excitation on phosphenes, if any, 2 'control' phosphene patterns of 2 subjects were followed up during a period of 6 months. There was considerable stability of their shape and of their mean excitation frequency. Sometimes the occurrence of one particular 'control' phosphene was found at 10 c./sec. and integers of this frequency. As a result of additional chemical excitation by mescaline, psilocybin and LSD (in one subject) the following effects were observed: (1) Temporary increase of the original 2 'control' patterns in intensity and bandwidth from +/- 13% up to 100%. (2) Production of a great number of new phosphene patterns or pictures (mostly with non-abstract shape) with large bandwith and intensity, disappearing in the first and last stages of chemical stimulation when switching off the additional electrical stimulation. (3) During electrical and maximum chemical stimulation the new drug-induced pictures prevailed and the 'control patterns' disappeared (observed with mescaline and psilocybin only). (4) If, during electrical stimulation, only the stimulation current is varied at a constant frequency, the shape of the induced patterns may vary. (5) If, during electrical-chemical stimulation, the bandwith is large (order of +/- 50% to 100%) the change of picture shape cannot be accomplished by changing the pulse current. On the assumption that each phosphene pattern is produced by a neuronal network with definable bandwith, a simple cybernetic model of phosphene generation can be devised. According to this model, a feedback or resonance effect exists if the follower of each applied pulse arrives at the input neuron of the chain not earlier than after the time tN, but at the latest after the time n-tN, where tN is the delay-time of one neuron, and 'n' an integer indicating the number of neurons in each particular chain. In contrast to models of 'objective' viewing, no inhibitory neuronal network elements are necessary. The realization of such a model is possible, for example, by substituting neurons with electromechanical relays which have switching delay times of the order of msec, ('coincidence circuit'). From the model it may also be concluded that the increase of excitation frequency bandwidth during additional chemical excitation may be due to the association of new chemically pre-excited neuronal chains (belonging to larger cortical fields) to the primary ensemble excitable by electrical stimulation only. This would be an analogue to Dusser de Barenne's and McCulloch's findings on the effect of strychninization of brain tissue.

tertiary_title: La psilocybine: Perspectives d'utilisation en psychiatrie clinique
author_address: M. Toscano Aguilar, 43 Ave Jacques Pastur, Bruxelles, Belgium
note: (Toscano Aguilar) 43 Ave Jacques Pastur, Bruxelles, Belgium
title: Psilocybin: Possibilities in clinical psychiatry
abstract: Psilocybin is a psychodysleptic drug. In small doses it has a marked psychotonic effect, which wears off after some time. Large doses always produce somatic effects, mostly psychic. An absence of psychic reaction seems to be obvious in cases with blunt affectivity and loss of temporal foresight. If psychic effects do occur, there is an intense emotional revival of hidden psychic contents and problems. At the same time psycho-sensitive alterations are perceived. If psychic contents could be recalled, the drug might be considered for use in analytical procedures. Psilocybin if psychically effective, creates an exceptional situation, which might be made use of in commencing psychotherapy. In this respect it seems to be most important that the patient should simultaneously be able to be actor and spectator in his own life history, because of the personality partition induced by the drug. As a dialogue is made possible between oneself and ones problem contents, it might, under therapeutic guidance, lead to an understanding of the behavioural trends and to a clear insight into the actual situation and the future prospects. In some cases, having discarded these structures of stereotype reaction, the patient might reach a new ego organization, by realising his vital needs. The technique of this form of psychotherapy is thoroughly described and the indications are made clear. The importance of this form of treatment is stressed in the case of criminal youths.

author_address: G. Honigfeld, VA Cent. NP Res. Lab., Perry Point, MD, United States
note: (Honigfeld) VA Cent. NP Res. Lab., Perry Point, MD, United States
title: Effect of an hallucinogenic agent on verbal behavior
abstract: Close analysis was used to assess the 'understandability' of the spontaneous speech of a normal subject who had received 9 mg. of psilocybin. This drug seemed to exert an enhancing effect within the first 1.5 hr., followed quickly by a deterioration in the quality of verbal communication for about the next 2 hr.

author_address: J.E. Steiner, Dcpt. of Appi, PharmacoL Hebrew Univ., Sch. of Pharm., Jerusalem
note: (Steiner, Suimaf) Dcpt. of Appi, PharmacoL Hebrew Univ., Sch. of Pharm., Jerusalem
title: SIMULTANEOUS STUDIES of BLOOD SUGAR, BEHAVIOURAL CHANGES and EEG on THE WAKE RABBIT after ADMINISTRATION of PSILOCYBIN
abstract: Significant transient changes in behaviour, accompanied by increase of blood sugar and EEG changes were noted. The latter included decrease of voltage and desynchronization of brain activity. The fact that all changes appeared simultaneously strengthens the theory of their causal connection. (II, 8*).

author_address: J.F. Brodey, Thudichum Psychiat. Res. Lab., Gale Sbur G State Res. Hosp., Galesburg, IL
note: (Brodey, Steiner, Himwich) Thudichum Psychiat. Res. Lab., Gale Sbur G State Res. Hosp., Galesburg, IL
title: An electrographic study of psilxcin and 4-methyl-alpha-methyl tryptamine (mp-809)
abstract: In this study 59 rabbits were used for an EEG analysis of 5 compounds: 0-phosphoryl-4-hydroxy-N-dimethyl tryptamine (psilocybin), 4-hydroxy-yV-dimethyl tryptamine (psilocin), 4-methyl-alpha-methyl tryptamine (MP-809), 4-hydroxy-alpha-methyl tryptamine (MP-14) and 1-methyl psilocybin. Four different preparations were employed, 2 involving transection of the brain and one of the cervical cord. In experiments on the intact brain groups of 6 rabbits were used and each of the 5 compounds was tested. The precollicular, prepontine preparation was employed in 10 rabbits to localize sites of action of MP-809 and psilocin. In other experiments involving the postcollicular,postpontine transection 15 animals were studied for additional information on the same 2 drugs. In addition, 4 animals having a transection at the level of the first cervical vertebra were used in a further study of psilocin. In rabbits with intact brain all 5 drugs produced EEG alert patterns. When MP-809 was administered to animals transected in a prepontine, precollicular plane only a slight lowering of amplitude was seen in the EEG pattern. But when one-third the dose of eserine needed to evoke sustained activation in an animal so transected was administered to animals pretreated with MP-809 a fully alert pattern was obtained indicating a site of minor action rostral to the midbrain and probably cholinergic in nature. When, however, MP-809 was administered to animals transected in a. pusicoilicuiar, postpontine plane the EEG pattern duplicated, with minor variations, the EEG arousal seen in intact animals. Thus a potent site of action for MP-809 was found in the midbrain, a region possessing a strong adrenergic component. Psilocin failed to evoke alert patterns in animals transected either rostral or caudal to the midbrain, thus excluding the midbrain and structures more rostrally situated as possible sites of action. On the other hand, animals injected with psilocin and subsequently transected at the level of the first cervical vertebra continued to display EEG alerting thus indicating a site of action below the midbrain but excluding the spinal cord. It is not likely that small changes in brain serotonin or in systemic blood pressure could account for the alterations in EEG produced by these 2 drugs.

author_address: E.K. Zsigmond, Depts of Anesthesiol, Univ. of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, PA, United States
note: (Zsigmond, Foldes, Folders) Depts of Anesthesiol, Univ. of Pittsburgh, Pittsburgh, PA, United States
title: The in vitro inhibitory effect of psilocybin and related compounds on human cholinesterases
abstract: The comparison of the anticholinesterase activity of psilocybin, bufotenin and 5hydroxytryptarnine in human plasma, red cells and gray matter homogenate indicates that like with LSD and its derivatives, there is no correlation between the in- vitro anticholinesterase activity and the hallucinogenic effect of these compounds.

tertiary_title: Considerazioni sugli stati psichici pre-schizofrenici
author_address: R. Citrolo, Clin. delle Mal. del Sist. Nerv., Univ. di Palermo
note: (Citrolo) Clin. delle Mal. del Sist. Nerv., Univ. di Palermo
title: Pre-schizophrenic conditions
abstract: This paper contains psycho-physiological digressions on schizophrenia, schizoid states and psychasthenia. Forty-one references.

tertiary_title: Auto-observation de deux intoxications experimentales par la Psilocybine
author_address: Cl. Wiart, Clin. de la Fac., Paris
note: (Wiart) Clin. de la Fac., Paris
title: Auto-observation of two experimental intoxications with psilocybin
abstract: A report of 2 oral auto-intoxications with 10 mg. of psilocybin. The first test with 2 observers present, aimed unsuccessfully at painting the visual phenomena. The second test was undertaken to obtain a better understanding of the problems of delirium. The tests were made at intervale of 2 months. The pertinent experiences, which are fundamentally different,are not described in their chronological appearance but as perceived and experienced phenomena (illusions, hallucinoses and hallucinations of the various sensory organs). These are then grouped as regards their formation and interconnection with the multiple influences of external reality, somatic modification, ideo-affectivity, and personality. An attempt is made to determine the level of consciousness of the intoxicated individual and to indicate the elements of belief which through the mediation of irrefutable certainty and a truly fertile moment bring about genuine, primary delirious experiences.

author_address: A. Christiansen, Dept. of Pharmacol., State Univ. of New York Upstate Med. Cent., Syracuse, NY, United States
note: (Christiansen, Baum, Witt) Dept. of Pharmacol., State Univ. of New York Upstate Med. Cent., Syracuse, NY, United States
journal_name: Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics
title: Changes in spider webs brought about by mescaline, psicocybin and an increase in body weight
abstract: 150 mg./kg. of psilocybin per os, 1 g./kg. of mescaline per os. or a 30% increase in body weight made spiders build webs the following day with a shorter thread. The weight increase also caused a thicker thread measured as higher nitrogen content per metre thread. This can be explained by assuming that the heavier spider has to build a thicker thread to hold its own weight while it has not enough material to build it of equal length. Removal of weight led only after 3 and more days to a return to thread thickness and length of control webs. However, these heavier spiders repeated their web-building at a normal frequency. The shorter thread after psilocybin application was not thicker nor were any changes in web proportions observed. Further increase in the dose of psilocybin caused a dose-dependent decrease in web-building frequency, and none out of 33 spiders which had received 6 g./kg. psilocybin built a web on the following day. This may be comparable to the relaxing effect of psilocybin in higher animals or be attributed to an effect on thread production. The mescaline webs with shorter threads also showed a smaller catching area and more irregular angles. A higher dose diminished web-building too. The ratio between effective doses of mescaline and psilocybin was about 1:10 measured as changes in thread length or web-building frequency, with psilocybin being the more potent drug.

author_address: R.D. Bunag, Dept. of Pharmacol., Univ. of Kansas Med. Cent., Kansas City, KS, United States
note: (Bunag, Walaszek) Dept. of Pharmacol., Univ. of Kansas Med. Cent., Kansas City, KS, United States
journal_name: Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics
title: Differential antagonism by BAS-phenol of responses to the indolealkylamines
abstract: Studies were made on the antagonistic effect of BAS-phenol on blood pressure responses of different animal species to various indolealkylamines. In the dog, BAS-phenol selectively blocks responses to serotonin, bufotenin, 4-hydroxytryptamine, psilocin and psilocybin but not those to tryptamine or dimethyltryptamine. A similar differentiation could usually be shown in the cat and the rabbit but not in the chicken. Differentiation between serotonin and tryptamine by selective specificity of BAS-phenol antagonism could not be demonstrated in the isolated guinea-pig ileum and rabbit ear preparations.

tertiary_title: Contributo clinico, elettroencefalografico e biologico allo studio della psilocibina
author_address: G. Gamna, Osp. Psichiat., Prov. di Torino
note: (Gamna, Gobbi, Ferrio, Rivolta, Gandiglio, Vercellino) Osp. Psichiat., Prov. di Torino
title: Clinical, EEG and biological data on psylocibine
abstract: The authors conducted 2 experiments to investigate the effects of psylocibine. The first concerned 5 chronic schizophrenics and 5 cases of affective depressive psychosis. Each was given 2 mg. and 8 mg. of the drug by mouth for 10 days. In the second a normally healthy volunteer and 10 patients suffering from various mental diseases were given 3 mg. of the drug by the i.v. route. Some EEG changes were observed in the second group. It is concluded that psylocibine may be of therapeutic value in some selected cases, and may be used for revealing psychopathological structures and some aspects of the patient's individuality.

tertiary_title: Recherche d'equivalents experimentaux au pouvoir hallucinogene. Action des hallucinogenes sur la temperature rectale du Lapin et sur les effets de la morphine chez la souris
author_address: J. Jacob, Serv. de Chim. Therapeut., Lab. de Pharmacol., Inst. Pasteur, Paris, France
note: (Jacob, Lafille, Loiseau, Echinard-Garin, Barthelemy) Serv. de Chim. Therapeut., Lab. de Pharmacol., Inst. Pasteur, Paris, France
title: Search for experimental equivalents of hallucinogenic activity. Effects of hallucinogens on rectal temperature in rabbit and on morphine effects in mouse
abstract: With lysergamide, bromolysergamide, psilocybin, dimethyl- and diethyltryptamines and mescaline, a satisfactory correlation exists between temperature raising (in rabbits), antianalgesic (in mice) and hallucinogenic (in men, according to the literature) potencies. The piperidyl diphenylglycolates were also found to raise the temperature in the rabbit but their hallucinogenic potencies were seemingly in closer relationship with a particular antagonism towards morphine in mice. For nalorphine - which which induces hypothermia in the rabbit - antianalgesic and hallucinogenic activities are in the same relationship as for the above-mentioned substances; amphetamine, and phencyclidine raised the rectal temperature of the rabbit but did not antagonize morphine. The results are discussed with regard to the catecholergic, tryptamine and cholinolytic hypotheses of mode of action of hallucinogenic drugs, and the value of the tests as screening and characterizing methods for such agents.

author_address: L.E. Hollister, Dept. Serv. for Res., Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hollister) Dept. Serv. for Res., Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
journal_name: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
title: Drug-induced psychoses and schizophrenic reactions: A critical comparison
abstract: Comparison of clinical syndromes from psychotomimetic drugs with schizophrenic reactions reveals some basic differences in particular symptoms but, most of all, in sum. Screened normal subjects given fixed doses of each of three psychotomimetics (mescaline, psilocybin, and LSD-25), using blind controls, reported a preponderance of somatic and perceptual effects and comparatively few psychopathologic symptoms of the type evident in schizophrenics. Dizziness, weakness, drowsiness, tremulousness, paraesthesias, and blurred vision were common, as were visual illusions and hallucinations. Disorientation, paranoid ideation, disturbed thinking, and auditory, gustatory, olfactory or tactile hallucinations were uncommon. With JB-329, a different picture was observed, characteristic of a toxic delirium. Another basis for comparing drug-induced psychoses and schizophrenic reactions was by means of brief taped interviews with 6 subjects under drugs (2 each on psilocybin, mescaline, and JB-329) and 6 schizophrenics. Using imperfect blind controls, 78 professional raters were able to judge the drug subjects correctly from 67 to 73 times, the schizophrenics correctly from 66 to 75 times. Thus it would appear that a reasonably experienced clinical observer should easily be able to distinguish the 2 conditions. In view of these considerable clinical differences between drug states and the naturally occurring psychosis, questions have been raised about the relevance of the former to the study of the latter.

author_address: D.W. Woolley, Rockefeller Inst., New York, NY, United States
note: (Woolley, Campbell) Rockefeller Inst., New York, NY, United States
title: Serotonin-like and antiserotonin properties of psilocybin and psilocin
abstract: These psychotomimetic analogues of serotonin act like this hormone in some tests and against it in others.

author_address: M.H. Wiseman-Distler, Allan Mem. Inst. of Psychiat., McGill Univ., Montreal, Que., Canada
note: (Wiseman-Distler, Sourkes) Allan Mem. Inst. of Psychiat., McGill Univ., Montreal, Que., Canada
journal_name: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
title: The effect of 4-hydroxyindoles on the metabolism of 5-hydroxytryptamine (serotonin)
abstract: Psilocybin does not have a direct effect on 5HT metabolism. The delay in excretion of 5HIAA observed after administration of a 5HT load may be attributed to the prolonged vasopressor activity of psilocybin. On the other hand psilocin does decrease the rate of 5HT breakdown in vitro. This is not as clearly demonstrable in vivo because of what appears to be an 'anti-5HT-pressor' effect of psilocin. Psilocybin does not cause any of the effects observed after treatment with psilocin. From this observation it may be inferred that if psilocybin and psilocin are in equilibrium in vivo the predominant direction of this equilibrium is toward psilocybin.

author_address: L.E. Hollister, Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hollister, Degan, Schultz) Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
title: An experimental approach to facilitation of psychotherapy by psychotomimetic drugs
abstract: From a controlled study of patients given mescaline, LSD-25 or psilocybin whilst undergoing psychotherapy it was concluded that there was no definite indication that psychotomimetic drugs facilitated psychotherapy, but it was considered that a further experimental approach was practicable.

author_address: Dept. of Child. Hlth., Univ. of Adelaide
note: (Maxwell, Kneebone, Elliott) Dept. of Child. Hlth., Univ. of Adelaide
journal_name: Archives internationales de pharmacodynamie et de therapie
title: The effect of psilocybin upon the systemic, pulmonary and coronary circulation of the intact dog
abstract: Circulatory effects of a known paychotomimetic agent, peilocybin, were investigated. In anaesthetized dogs psilocybin in a dosage of 0.5 mg./kg. intravenously, depresses respiration and arterial O2 saturation, possibly deepening the anaesthesia. Psilocybin is a sympathomimetic agent, and raises blood pressure, heart rate, and pulmonary and peripheral vascular resistance. Coronary resistance remains unchanged, while blood flow increases significantly owing to the raised blood pressure. The efficiency of the heart becomes somewhat diminished. Cardiovascular effects of psilocybin are similar to those of serotonin, this being in accordance with the weak anti-serotonin effect of psilocybin.

author_address: A.B. Wolbach Jr., Nat. Inst. of Med. Hlth., Addiction Res. Cent., U. S. Publ. Hlth. Serv. Hosp., Lexington, KY, United States
note: (Wolbach Jr., Isbell, Miner) Nat. Inst. of Med. Hlth., Addiction Res. Cent., U. S. Publ. Hlth. Serv. Hosp., Lexington, KY, United States
title: Cross tolerance between mescaline and LSD-25 with a comparison of the mescaline and LSD reactions
abstract: Reactions caused by i. m. administration of 0.75 mug./kg. and 1.5 mug./kg. of lysergide (LSD) were compared with those caused by mescaline (2.5 and 5.0 mg./kg.) in the same 10 subjects. Both drugs caused pupil dilatation, rise of temperature, pulse rate and systolic blood pressure, and lowering of threshold for elicitation of the knee-jerk. Similar abnormal mental states (anxiety, difficulty in thinking, mood changes - generally euphoric, altered sensory perception - particularly visual, and alterations of body image) were reported by the subjects after both drugs. Effects of mescaline appeared more slowly and persisted somewhat longer than those of lysergide. Weight for weight, lysergide tartrate is 2400-4900 times as potent as mescaline; on a molecular basis lysergide is 4500-9275 times as potent as mescaline. Patients receiving lysergide daily developed direct tolerance to lysergide and were also cross-tolerant to mescaline, and vice versa. It is inferred that lysergide,psilocybin and mescaline probably share common mechanisms of action or some common final pathway.

author_address: W.R. Adey, Brain Res. Inst., Univ. of California, Los Angeles, CA, United States
note: (Adey, Bell, Dennis) Brain Res. Inst., Univ. of California, Los Angeles, CA, United States
title: Effects of LSD-25, psilocybin and psilocin on temporal lobe EEG patterns and learned behavior in the cat
abstract: The effects of LSD-25, psilocybin and psilocin were studied in 18 cats with electrodes chronically implanted in the amygdala, parts of the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex, the anterior ventral thalamus, rostral midbrain reticular formation and the primary visual cortex. Electrical seizure-like activity was seen which was in part dependent on dosage but probably had its maximal effect in the dorsal hipocampus and entorhinal cortex; the seizures seemed to be critically dependent on the reduction of visual and auditory sensory influence but were frequently associated with the ingestion of food. Tolerance to LSD appeared when doses were repeated at intervals more frequent than 7-10 days. Psilocybin and psilocin had the same general effects as LSD-25.

title: Mescaline, lysergic acid diethylamide and psilocybin: Comparison of clinical syndromes, effects on colour perception and biochemical measures
abstract: Mescaline, lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD-25) and psilocybin were studied in 20 screened subjects, 18 of them receiving all 3 drugs. Drugs were administered under similar test conditions, doses were constant as between drugs and subjects, assignments to drugs followed a latin-square sequence, and subjects were unaware of the drug given at each trial. Clinical syndromes were assessed by a questionnaire completed by the subjects after each drug trial. Colour perception was studied by means of both adequate and inadequate stimuli for eliciting colour phenomena, measurements being taken before and 2 hours after the drug was administered. A number of selected biochemical and physiological measurements were also made at similar times. Clinical syndromes were comparable in kind and degree for all 3 drugs, that from mescaline being most pronounced. Somatic manifestations predominated, psychotomimetic symptoms (other than visual hallucinations) being relatively uncommon. Colour perception was not altered much when adequate stimuli were used, but colour phenomena were appreciably enhanced from inadequate stimuli. Minor differences in colour perceptual effects were noted between the 3 drugs, but similarities were greater. Each of the 3 drugs significantly decreased urinary excretion of inorganic phosphorus, increased plasma free fatty acids and decreased total circulating eosinophils. Of the other biochemical measurements made, only one other significant change was noted: an increase in copper oxidase activity after psilocybin. The 3 psychotomimetic drugs were quite comparable in the areas studied. One might assume that they have many common mechanisms of action despite their chemical differences.

author_address: B. Wilkens, Dept. of Exp. Psychiat., New York State Psychiat. Inst., New York, NY, United States
note: (Wilkens, Malitz, Esecover) Dept. of Exp. Psychiat., New York State Psychiat. Inst., New York, NY, United States
title: Clinical observations of simultaneous hallucinogen administration in identical twins
abstract: Different initial affective responses occurred in identical twins wider the influence of D-LSD-25 and psilocybin. These affective displays were related to the differences in personality between the twins. It was possible for the affectivity of each twin to influence the affective response of the other at various times during the studies. This communication of affect substantiates the hypothesis that affective responses associated with hallucinogen administration are personality-specific rather than drug-specific. The drug-specific changes in the autonomic, proprioceptive and perceptual spheres were similar in both twins and not modified to any noticeable extent by environmental influences. Because of their profound effects, hallucinogens should be restricted to research use exclusively in a hospital setting. Their use at this time for any other purpose or in any other setting is dangerous.

author_address: A.B. Wolbach, Addiction Res. Cent., Publ. Hlth Serv. Hosp., Lexington, KY
note: (Wolbach, Miner, Isbell) Addiction Res. Cent., Publ. Hlth Serv. Hosp., Lexington, KY
title: Comparison of psilocjn with psilocybin, mkscalink and lsd-25
abstract: A dose of 1 mug./kg. of lysergide tartarate is approximately equivalent to 45 mug./kg. of psilocin; 1 mug./kg. of psilocin is equivalent to 66 mug./kg. of mescaline. Psilocin is approximately 1.4 times as potent as psilocybir. PopoviC - Bratislava.

author_address: R. Fischer, Columbus Psychiat. Inst., Ohio State Univ., Columbus, OH, United States
note: (Fischer, Griffin, Mead) Columbus Psychiat. Inst., Ohio State Univ., Columbus, OH, United States
title: Two characteristic ranges of taste sensitivity
abstract: Subjects characterized by very high taste-thresholds for 6-n-propylthiouracil and quinine also display high taste-thresholds for a wide variety of chemically unrelated compounds, such as chlorpromazine, psilocybin, sodium chloride, etc. etc., whereas a combination of low thresholds for 6-n-propylthiouracil and quinine is characteristic fut subjects with low thresholds for a wide variety of other compounds. The saliva of subjects with very high taste-thresholds for 6-n-propylthiouracil ('non-tasters') oxidized in vivo certain compounds, e.g. chlorpromazine, at a faster rate than the saliva of (sensitive) tasters of 6-n-propylthiouracil. The possibility that the reported two ranges of taste sensitivity may (1) also express systemic differences in drug responsiveness and (2) be a factor involved in the relation between taste-thresholds and food dislike, is discussed.

tertiary_title: Etude clinique et polygraphique d'un nouveau type de psycho-dysleptique: Le ditran
author_address: J. Delay, ParisFrance
title: Clinical and polygraphic study of a new type of psychodysleptic: 'Ditran'
abstract: This is an entirely synthetic product. It causes a remarkably constant syndrome in all subjects. After slow i. v. injection 4 stages can be distinguished. (1) Immediately after the injection autonomie disturbances develop, in the first place tachycardia and respiratory disorders. The duration of these symptoms is rather constant; they rapidly disappear after half an hour. (2) Very early - after a latency period of 10-20 min. - pyramidal symptoms develop. These persist for several hours. (3) After a phase of profound obnubilation, confusion and oneirism develop. These appear at the same time as the first autonomie phenomena and may persist in the form of an oneiric delirium for 12-24 hr. (4) A change in mood, viz. an expansive post-oneiric euphoria. The dysleptic and autonomic effects of ditran do not appear to be influenced by previous neuroleptic treatment. Tetrahydro-aminoacridine has a potent and immediate effect on the syndrome induced by ditran. This effect was verified by polygraphy and mainly involved the autonomic changes and the state of wakefulness. The effect of ditran thus differs from that of other dysleptics in current use. The severity of the somatic changes it produces resembles shock therapy. Similar effects have been observed by Sigwald after the administration of a phenothiazine derivative (7369 RP). The relatively poor oneiric experience contrasts with the great variety of sensations induced by mescaline, psilocybin and LSD 25.

author_address: L.E. Hollister, Med. and Psychiat. Serv., Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hollister, Prusmack, Paulsen, Rosenquist) Med. and Psychiat. Serv., Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
journal_name: Journal of Nervous and Mental Disease
title: Comparison of three psychotropic drugs (psilocybin, JB-329, and it-290) in volunteer subjects
abstract: Three new paychotropic drugs, psilocybin, IT 290 (DL-alpha-methyltryptamine) and JB 329 ('ditran') were compared in volunteer subjects. Psilocybin resembled lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD-25), producing a clinical syndrome of anxiety, euphoria, introspection and visual effects lasting about 4 hr. IT 290 more closely resembled amphetamine in producing mood elevation and reserpine in producing somatic effects. Effects of large acute doses persisted for 12 or more hours. JB 329 resembled ecopolamine, producing a toxic delirium lasting 12 to 24 hr. Total circulating eosinophils were significantly reduced by both psilocybin and JB 329. Psilocybin also reduced urinary excretion of inorganic phosphorus. IT 290 had no effect on either of these biochemical tests. None of the other tests measured (serum alkaline phosphatase, serum pseudocholinesterase and serum glutamic oxalacetic transaminase activity, or serum cholesterol) were altered by either drug. EEG tracings showed no clinically detectable changes. Psychometric tests revealed a decrement from psilocybin suggesting decreased motivation. A larger impairment from JB 329 was attributed to decreased performance. IT 290 did not change the tests significantly, though tending to increase both motivation and performance. Chronic administration of JB 329 leads to tolerance.

author_address: D.R. Curtis, Dept. of Physiol., Australian Nat. Univ., Canberra, ACT, Australia
note: (Curtis, Davis) Dept. of Physiol., Australian Nat. Univ., Canberra, ACT, Australia
title: A central action of 5-hydroxytryptamine and noradrenaline
abstract: When introduced extracellularly by an electrophoretic technique into the lateral geniculate body the following substances (in descending order of activity) reversibly inhibited orthodromic impulses but not antidromic impulses: serotonin, tryptamine, bufotenin, lysergide, psilocin, psilocybin, 3-hydroxytyramine, noradrenaline, adrenaline and bromolysergide. Creatinine and glutamic acid had no effect. Glutamic acid and psilocybin were introduced as anions at pH 8 and the other substances as cations at pH 4.

tertiary_title: Klinische erfahrungen mit psilocybin (cy 39 sandoz)
author_address: M. Sercl, Neurol. Klin., Karls-Univ., Hradec Kralove, Czech Republic
note: (Sercl, Kovarik, Jaros) Neurol. Klin., Karls-Univ., Hradec Kralove, Czech Republic
title: Clinical experiences with psilocybin
abstract: A study of the effect of psilocybin on 15 healthy subjects was conducted: the dosage was 1 to 2 mg. orally or 3 to 6 mg. subcutaneously. Subsequently this drug was administered to 30 neurotic patients in small daily doses of 1 to 2 mg. orally or 3 mg. subcutaneously. The effect of the drug was assessed in all cases by means of placebo administration. In the low doses used, psilocybin produced a euphoric reaction without affecting the underlying neurological condition. The euphoric effect is a great aid to psychotherapy. In a number of cases the drug favourably influences those depressive states which are a consequence of organic disease of the nervous system. The reaction to psilocybin varies from one individual to another. Its effect on a given patient depends largely on his mood at the particular time. The development of tolerance or addiction has not been observed.

tertiary_title: Untersuchungen mit psilocybin, einer psychotropen substanz aus psilocybe Mexicana
author_address: W. Rummele, Psychiat. Klin., Univ. und Pharmakol. Lab., Sandoz AG, Basel, Switzerland
note: (Rummele, Cnirss) Psychiat. Klin., Univ. und Pharmakol. Lab., Sandoz AG, Basel, Switzerland
journal_name: Schweizer Archiv fur Neurologie, Neurochirurgie und Psychiatrie
title: Experiments with psilocybin, a psychotropic substance from psilocybe Mexicana
abstract: The reaction induced by a single dose of psilocybin has been observed in 18 trials, the drug having been administered orally and subcutaneously in an equal number of cases. A dose of 6 mg. of psilocybin proved to produce definite mental effects without severe physical disturbances. During a first phase of intoxication, activity was diminished; during the second phase, an increase in activity together with a prevailing euphoric, rarely dysphoric moodiness occurred. About half of the subjects reported an altered sensory perception, less often a feeling of depersonalization. With parenteral administration marked autonomic effects occurred, such as bradycardia, increased blood pressure, respiratory changes, diminution in respiratory rate and increase in respiratory volume, headache and vertigo. One of the cases given 10 mg. of psilocybin parenterally showed marked autonomic disturbance, elementary hallucinations and a feeling of depersonalization.

tertiary_title: La psilocybine. See implications therapeutiques
title: Psilocybine - Its therapeutic aspects
abstract: A report is submitted of a clinical study in which psilocybine was used in oneiro-analysis. This study was carried out on 47 normal subjects and 90 mental patients; the substance was administered orally or by i. m. injections, in a dosage of 9-14 mg. The drug had a pronounced neuro-vegetative effect on normal subjects as well as on patients. Mydriasis, changes in the pulse and unstable blood pressure were commonly observed. The mental effects in normal subjects differed from those observed in the patients. Experimental intoxication with psilocybine caused a cycle of manifestations which lasted 4 hr., with a maximal intensity around the 2nd hr. The first sign was a change in mood and in activity; subsequently there appeared alterations of perception, illusions, visual hallucinations and disturbances of consciousness. In the mental patients, the drug intensified the manifestations of the psychosis or the underlying neurosis, so that they were easier to identify. The therapeutic effect of psilocybine was twofold: biological and psychological. The psychological effect was due to the utilization of the material provided during the attack, and to the modifications of the relationship between the physician and the patient.

tertiary_title: Onkiserlet psilocybinnel
title: Auto-experiment with psilocybine
abstract: The pharmacopsychiatric effect of dimethyl- and diethyltryptamine and psilocybine was studied. The author consumed during the experiment 9 mg. psilocybine per os and observed subsequently vegetative symptoms, temporary writing troubles, tachycardia and strong tremor, hyperaesthesia of the sense of touch, euphoria, temporary dominance of the first signalling system, illusions and pseudohallucinations. Psilocybine produced synaesthetic experiences in a smaller degree than diethyltryptamine. These experiences were not diffused over the entire sensorial sphere as was the case with diethyltryptamine tests, and hypnagogic visions did not follow the rhythm of sound stimuli. During the entire experiment, self-control was always maintained. Vivid 'lilliput' visions and periodical troubles of consciousness explain the cultic practices of primitives who attribute a 'divinative', 'clairvoyant' effect to this drug.

author_address: Psychiat. Univ.-Klin., Waldau-Bern
note: (Heimann) Psychiat. Univ.-Klin., Waldau-Bern
title: Expressive phenomena in model psychoses (psilocybin), a comparison with self-depicting and loss of psychic function
abstract: The author sets out the method of studying expressive phenomena by the use of sound-film recording. He also describes its application to model psychoses and illustrates this with a report on the preliminary findings as to the effect of the new phantasticum, called psilocybin The expressive change can be divided into 3 phases, which indicate that the drug exerts its effect progressively on ego-distant and ego-proximal areas of the person's basic constitution. Changes in basic condition as deduced from expression correspond closely to those deduced from the person's actual experiences.Comparison of impairment in concentration reveals that this is at its maximum in the phases accompanied by least expressive change (phases 1 and 2) and at a minimum in the 3rd phase, which exhibits the maximum expressive change. Memory performance is uninfluenced but verbal facility is equally impaired in all 3 phases. The findings show that the drug takes effect at different levels and takes time to reach its full effect. Any analogy between model psychoses and genuine psychoses remains doubtful. Exact registration and interpretation of expression and behaviour can provide a reliable basis both for the appropriate application of other psychological tests and for discriminating judgments on the relationship between model and genuine psychoses.

author_address: L.E. Hollister, Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
note: (Hollister) Vet. Adm. Hosp., Palo Alto, CA, United States
journal_name: Archives internationales de pharmacodynamie et de therapie
title: Clinical, biochemical and psychologic effects of psilocybin
abstract: Psilocybin was tested on 16 normal volunteers, 9 subjects receiving both oral (60-200 mug./kg.) and s. c. (37-203 mug./kg.) doses. Psilocybin has a shorter span of action than lysergide or mescaline, peak effects occurring between 90 and 120 min. after medication. It is more agreeable to subjects than lysergide and produces dreamy states without marked impairment of faculties. Pupillary dilatation and increased deep tendon reflexes were constantly observed. Inorganic phosphorus excretion and total eosinophils were reduced. In the psychomimetic field, psilocybin decreased motivation, but did not influence accuracy.

title: Controlled sensory input: A note on the technic of drug evaluation with a preliminary report on a comparative study of sernyl, psilocybin, and LSD-25
abstract: Sensory attenuation, a modified form of sensory deprivation where sensory inputs are controlled, is described as a method useful for the study of drug responses. The above is a preliminary report about a comparative study, using this technique, of the following 3 psychotomimetic drugs: (1) sernyl 1, (1-phenylcyclohexyl)piperidine monohydrochloride (May and Baker C 1395); (2) psilocybin, a tryptamine derivative: isolated active principle of Psilocybe mexicana heim, a Mexican mushroom (Sandoz); (3) LSD-25, D-lysergic acid diethylamide (Sandoz).

title: Comparative effects of the administration of taraxein, d-LSD, mescaline, and psilocybin to human volunteers
abstract: This study is a comparison of the effects induced in 4 nonpsychotic volunteer subjects with the administration of various psychotomimetic agents. Taraxein induced symptoms which the examiners considered to closely approximate those seen with endogenous schizophrenia. Following administration of taraxein, there was more dysphoria, blocking and thought deprivation displayed than with the other psychotomimetic compounds. Clear-cut secondary symptoms evolved with the administration of taraxein which were more typical of those seen in schizophrenic patients than the secondary symptoms induced by the other compounds. The changes induced with the administration of the other compounds were more typically toxic. Outstanding features were disturbances in sensory perception, particularly visual distortions, giddiness, and euphoria.

author_address: S. Malitz, Dept. of Exp. Psychiat., New York State Psychiat. Inst., New York, NY, United States
note: (Malitz, Esecover, Wilkens, Hoch) Dept. of Exp. Psychiat., New York State Psychiat. Inst., New York, NY, United States
title: Some observations on psilocybin, a new hallucinogen, in volunteer subjects
abstract: Fourteen paid volunteers, screened by clinical interviews, received psilocybin orally over a dosage range of 8 to 36 mg. The perceptual, affective, cognitive, behavioural and autonomic responses observed were qualitatively similar to those previously described with D-LSD 25, but quantitatively, a greater impairment of cognition with psilocybin was noted which may have been related either to dosage or to personality differences. EEG findings in 4 out of 8 subjects were similar to those previously reported with D-LSD 25 and mescaline. The use of psychotomimetic drugs as therapeutic agents in an out-patient setting may prove to be potentially hazardous. Acute stages of excitement, depression with suicidal ideation and impairment of judgment may occur with these drugs, even in the most carefully supervised in-patient setting. With out-patients, the danger of self-administration and inadequate supervision could combine and increase such occurrences. Further research is indicated regarding the site of action of hallucinogens, the relationship between personality, dosage level and total behavioural pattern, and the possible prognostic value of such drugs in assessing ego strength in specific individuals.

tertiary_title: Psilocybin, nove fantastikum
author_address: Psychiat. Klin. KU, Praha
note: (Roubicek, Drvota) Psychiat. Klin. KU, Praha
title: Psilocybin - A new phantasticum
abstract: Psilocybin is a psychotrophic hallucinogenic substance prepared from the Mexican fungus Psilocybe mexicana Heim, isolated in the Sandoz laboratories in crystalline form. In milligramme doses it produces a psychotic condition lasting several hours, characterized by sensory hallucinations, marked depersonalizations, signs of hypomania and euphoria with conditions of 'beatitude' with a loss of interest in the environment, disorders in perception of space, and time and other less regular psychic changes. It is associated with the following somatic symptoms: mydriasis, tendon hyperreflexia, bradycardia, fatigue. In about one-third of intoxicated persons there are uncomfortable vegetative symptoms, vertigo, nausea, tremor, perspiration - all these symptoms being mild. In the EEG there are mild signs of desynchronization, sometimes a more rapid alpha-rhythm, a decrease of its amplitude and a general flattening of the curve and an increase of beta-waves. As compared with other known hallucinogens, particularly mescalin and LSD 25, there are many similarities and some differences. The depersonalization after psilocybin is not so intense, the altered perception of space, is, however, more marked, the 'good humour and feeling of happiness' is more marked, while the vegetative symptoms are milder. The authors summarize the comparison in a table. Personal experiences (autointoxication) are described in detail and supplemented by drawings made during the intoxication and immediately after it. The drawings contain characteristic manifestations of geometrical and ornamental stylization with motifs of concentric zones with a loose composition whirly changes of pictures which are difficult to perceive, with disproportions of figural motifs with a disintegration of the body composition, with mutually penetrating ideas.

tertiary_title: A propos de l'utilisation des substances dysleptiquee en psychotherapie. Resultats favorables de seances repetees
title: The use of dysleptic substances in psychotherapy. Favourable results of repeated sessions
abstract: The use of psychodysleptic substances is suggested in individual psychotherapy of neurotics. A description is given of the use of psychodysleptics on the same patient, during 27 consecutive weekly sessions; the substances used were psilocybine (6 times), mescaline (11 times) and LSD (10 times). The 30-year-old patient had, at the end of his adolescence, exhibited symptoms of anxiety with a schizoid basis, character disorders and great difficulties in social adaptation. Although he partly benefited from psychoanalysis (classical Freudian method), he suffered from social and affective maladaptations, feelings of inferiority, insomnia (mild, without dreams) and myospasms. Dysleptic medication, particularly with mescaline, had an interesting effect. Progressive improvement was seen; his field of activity is greatly extended and his social conduct has become normalized.

author_address: P.K. Gessner, Res. Div., Cleveland Clin. Found, and Frank E. Bunts Educ. Inst., Cleveland. OH, United States
note: (Gessner, Khairallah, Mclsaac, Page) Res. Div., Cleveland Clin. Found, and Frank E. Bunts Educ. Inst., Cleveland. OH, United States
journal_name: Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics
title: The relattonship between the metabolic fate and pharmacological actions of serotonin. bufotenine and psilocybin
abstract: Bufotenine and psilocybin both possess a vasopressor activity in anaesthetized rats which is similar to that of serotonin and which can be blocked by bromolysergide. The duration of the pressor action is, however, greater, namely 30 min., with bufotenine and more than 1 hr. with psilocybin. The duration of the pressor activity is proportional and probably related to the rate at which these compounds are inactivated by monoamine oxidase in the in-vitro experiments. Experiments in vivo confirm that bufotenine and psilocybin are much less readily destroyed by monoamine oxidase than is serotonin; and that the alternative pathways of metabolism, namely excretion unchanged or in conjugation with glucuronic acid, are of more importance. The potentiatior. of hexobarbital sleeping times indicates that cardiovascular effects are paralleled by a central effect. The potentiation was 58%. 75% and 126% for serotonin, bufotenine and psilocybin, respectively. Unusual toxic effects characterized by weight loss and spinal kyphosis were found to occur 7 to 10 days after doses of 125 and 100 mg. kg. of bufotenine and psilocybin, respectively.

title: STUDIES on PSILOCYBIN and RELATED COMPOUNDS. I. COMMUNICATION. STRUCTURE/ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP of OXYINDOLEDERIVATIVES with REGARD to THEIR EFFECT on THE KNEE JERK of SPINAL CATS
abstract: The 4-hydroxyindole derivatives psilocybin and psllocin show a characteristic stimulatory effect on the patellar reflex of spinal cats. This is in contrast to the action of the 5-hydroxyindole derivatives bufotenin and serotonin, which temporarily block the patellar reflex. Using this criterion, a study on structure/activity relationship within a group of about 30 similar indoles was carried out, showing that stimulation of the knee jerk is limited to 4-substituted derivatives of dimethyltryptamine. (II, 8*).

journal_name: Bulletin de l'Academie nationale de medecine
title: The new chemotherapy in psychiatry. Results and statistics
abstract: The results of the therapy of mental disorders in children during the last 7 yr. are given statistically. The medicaments are divided into 3 groups: psycholeptics, psychoanaleptics and psychodysleptics. Among the newer psycholeptics, the so-called new neuroleptics are mentioned, including the group of chlor pro mazine and the Rauwolfia preparations. They induce the psycho motor syndrome. After the use of neuroleptics, the number of patients admitted diminished, and the excitative and restless states almost completely disappeared. They had a good influence in the maniacal, hypomaniacal and hallucinatory states, and also in schizophrenia. Psychoanaleptics were useful in the depressive and the melancholic states. Beside the different amines, derivatives of isonicotinic acid and iminodibenzyl (imipramine) are available. The author emphasizes the effectiveness of the combined therapy with imipramine and some of the neuroleptics, as for instance laevomepromazine. Among the psychodysleptics, the author mentions psilocybine, a hallucinogenic drug, whose formula resembles that of serotonin. It produces a dissolution of the mental synthesis, and a liberation of psychological automatism. The author's opinion is that this drug is useful in the new type of psychotherapy which is called chemical psychoanalysis. It is of great value in the therapy of the different neuroses.

tertiary_title: Effet therapeutique de la psilocybine sur une nevrose convulsive
title: Therapeutic effect of psilocybin on convulsive neurosis
abstract: The first trial, carried out under the influence of chlorpromazine, caused no emotional abreaction or affective reliving. It merely permitted the patient to express, in euphoric mood, her fundamental aspiration: to be freed from her body. In the second patient, without chlorpromazine, it caused a rush of memories. Without any control and with extreme violence, she explained what she thought to be the psychogenesis of her complaint, and especially her grievances against her mother. Childhood memories forgotten until then were emotionally relived, in particular her separation from the person she considered as her second mother. The first episode of anorexia at about the age of 6 was thus explained. It was this second injection of psilocybin which brought about the definitive recovery of the patient. The coming aware, intellectually and affectively, of her problems, as well as the lasting transformation of her attitude of mind, seem to have been the determining elements of this change.

title: Psilocybin, a new psychotropic substance
abstract: Psilocybe mexicana Heim belongs to the group of Mexican stimulating fungi, used mainly for religious rites. Pharmacologically, it has been neglected for centuries. The Swiss chemist A. Hofmann has isolated from this herb the substance Psilocybin, which he later, in 1958, succeeded in preparing synthetically. It is a phosphorus-containing indole derivative. The psychotropic actions of this substance have been determined in numerous experiments. They involve the perceptive sphere, affectivity and mood. No somatic side effects of significance have so far been observed. It is as yet an open question whether this substance will prove valuable therapeutically.

title: The effect of the action of psilocybin on the rabbit brain
abstract: Psilocybin, the by-product of which ('psilocin') has been identified as 4-hydroxydimethyl-tryptamine (4-HTP), develops in the waking rabbit a marked activation of the somatic behaviour and of the electrical brain activity. This stimulating action is due to a depression of the mediothalamic recruiting and moderating system rather than to an activation of the reticular arousal system. The electrophysiological effects of 4-HTP are compared with those of 5-HTP.

title: Psilocybin, a psychotropic active substance from the mexican narcotic mushroom psilocybe mexicana heim
abstract: This Psilocybe species has been cultivated and the active component extracted from the fruit body and the sclerotium. Chromatographically, 2 fractions were separated and by further purification 2 different substances were obtained. The elementary composition of the first one, called psilocybin, is C13H18(20)O3N2P2. As a UV spectrum it shows the characteristics of an indole derivative with substitution on the benzene nucleus. The 2nd substance, psilocin, is very unstable and has not yet been analysed. An oral dose of 4-8 mg. of psilocybin produces in human subjects a state of hypnosis somewhat similar to that with mescaline and lasting several hours.

title: Pharmacology of psilocybin, a drug from psilocybe mexicana heim
abstract: Psilocybin does not produce any characteristic effects on isolated organs, but in the intact mouse it causes mydriasis and piloerection in doses of not less than 10 mg./kg. s.c. In the unanaesthetized rabbit a dose of 1 mg./kg. i.v. suffices to cause mydriasis, tachycardia, tachypnoea and rise of temperature. The picture as a whole is that of central sympathetic stimulation, although the depression of motor activity does not agree with this.
